body: The bankruptcy court in the Northern District of Georgia has confirmed a Chapter 11 plan for New Grant Acquisitions, LLC, according to Bankruptcy Observer's docket brief for Nov. 20. The brief, which the outlet says was written by an AI agent from the court docket, reports that an order approving the disclosure statement and confirming the debtor's Fifth Amended Plan of Reorganization was entered Nov. 19 (Dkt. 259) before Judge Paul W. Bonapfel. The debtor had filed the Fifth Amended Plan that morning (Dkt. 256).

Creditor UC Grant Building Holder, LLC filed a notice of appeal to the district court within the hour (Dkt. 260), the brief reports. It followed with an emergency motion for a stay pending appeal (Dkt. 261) and an emergency motion to expedite briefing, argument and a ruling on the stay request (Dkt. 262). The brief does not describe the plan's terms or report a ruling on either motion.

In a Jan. 29, 2026 release, Hilco Global said it was accepting offers for the Grant Building, which it described as a 125,000± SF, 10-story site at 44 Broad Street in Atlanta's Fairlie-Poplar district, and that the sale was being conducted subject to approval by order of the bankruptcy court in Case No. BK 25-61599-PWB, the case number the docket brief gives for New Grant Acquisitions.

timeline.label: Hilco Global announces it is accepting offers for the Grant Building, with the sale subject to bankruptcy court approval in Case No. BK 25-61599-PWB

Order entered approving the disclosure statement and confirming the debtor's Fifth Amended Plan (Dkt. 259); UC Grant Building Holder, LLC files a notice of appeal (Dkt. 260), followed by emergency motions for a stay pending appeal and to expedite (Dkts. 261, 262)
